name: Benoxaprofen

own_problems.text: Pulled from the market worldwide, first in 1982 — for kidney harm, stomach and gut problems and blood problems

similar.name: Naproxen
problems: Carries a boxed warning in United States — for heart harm, stomach and gut problems and nerve and brain harm

similar.name: Pirprofen
problems: Pulled from the market worldwide, first in 1990 — for liver harm and stomach and gut problems

similar.name: Flurbiprofen
problems: Carries a boxed warning in United States — for heart harm, stomach and gut problems and nerve and brain harm

summary: Benoxaprofen was pulled from the worldwide market starting in 1982 because of kidney damage (nephrotoxicity), stomach or gut harm (gastrointestinal harm), and blood damage (hematological harm) [3]. A small computer model, rather than tests on people, calculated a high risk score for liver harm and a low risk score for heart harm [M]. Other drugs with similar chemical structures have also been pulled from the market or carry severe boxed warnings in the United States for harm to the stomach and gut, heart, liver, and nervous system (neurotoxicity) [4][5][6].
